nodes.name: Coula nut tree
nodes.desc: A rainforest tree with very hard nuts. Taï chimpanzees crack such nuts open with stones and branches.

nodes.name: Panda nut tree
nodes.desc: A tall forest tree whose oily nuts are among the hardest foods in the forest.

nodes.name: Ebony trees
nodes.desc: Ebony relatives of the forest understorey. GloBI records show monkeys eating the fruit of Diospyros soubreana.

nodes.name: Trichoscypha
nodes.desc: Forest trees with fleshy fruit. GloBI records show several monkeys and a forest mouse feeding on them.

nodes.name: Xylopia
nodes.desc: Pepper-fruit trees of the forest. GloBI records show Xylopia quintasii eaten by red colobus, Diana monkeys and mangabeys.

nodes.name: Western red colobus
nodes.desc: A leaf- and fruit-eating monkey of the high canopy. Wikipedia calls it a frequent prey of chimpanzees.

nodes.name: Diana monkey
nodes.desc: Eats mainly fruit, flowers and leaves in all levels of the canopy. Its predator-specific alarm calls are understood by other forest species.

nodes.name: Sooty mangabey
nodes.desc: A ground-and-canopy monkey of West African forest. GloBI records show it feeding on several Taï forest fruits.

nodes.name: Black duiker
nodes.desc: A small forest antelope of the undergrowth that eats fallen fruit and leaves.

nodes.name: Pygmy hippopotamus
nodes.desc: A secretive forest hippo that eats ferns, herbs and fallen fruit. Wikipedia lists Taï as one of the few areas holding it in Côte d'Ivoire.

nodes.name: African forest elephant
nodes.desc: Eats bark, leaves and many fruits, and spreads large seeds far across the forest. Taï numbers have fallen sharply since the 1970s.

nodes.name: Black-casqued hornbill
nodes.desc: Lives on fruit, mainly figs and oil palm fruits, and spreads seeds of many canopy trees.

nodes.name: Western chimpanzee
nodes.desc: Taï chimpanzees crack hard nuts with tools and hunt other primates, including red colobus. The subspecies is Critically Endangered.

nodes.name: African rock python
nodes.desc: A large forest snake. Wikipedia names a rock python among predators of young pygmy hippos.

nodes.name: African golden cat
nodes.desc: A shy forest cat that hunts small to medium animals such as duikers and rodents.

nodes.name: Leopard
nodes.desc: The top ground predator of Taï. Preys on duikers, monkeys and young pygmy hippos.

nodes.name: Crowned eagle
nodes.desc: At Taï monkeys make up over 60% of the remains at its nests, and about half of its guenon prey were Diana monkeys.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Light is scarce on the forest floor, so tall trees race for the canopy.

nodes.name: Year-round rain
nodes.desc: About 1,700 to 2,200 mm falls each year. The south has no real dry season.

nodes.name: Forest soil
nodes.desc: Thin, leaf-litter-fed soil; nutrients cycle fast in the humid forest.

nodes.name: Dung beetles & fungi
nodes.desc: Dung beetles, fungi and microbes break down dung, carcasses and fallen leaves and return nutrients to the soil.
